steps.name: Third: organize goals and initiatives on the Star Chart
steps.done_when: For a new mother ship, start in Star Chart with Aladdin as default steward; choose a dev-drive storage directory when available or another location, brainstorm major goals and their initiatives/deliverables, identify source material, and require at least one goal/initiative before previewing populated Star Chart and Cave. Existing-host clients reuse its organization.

steps.name: First: choose or connect to the mother ship
steps.done_when: On first launch choose this computer as the personal mother ship or connect to an existing personal host through a guided Tailscale and secure pairing-token flow. Install Anchor and Foundry skills only on a new mother ship; client devices use that host.

steps.name: Provider capacity, cost and model controls
steps.done_when: Carry cumulative Setup requirements into interactive Refinement 2: post-completion upper-left gear reopens existing Setup settings; Cave left sidebar bottom exposes the selected provider/account and model/reasoning through the same provider surface, with right-side capacity retained. Preserve host pairing, account tests and allowances, accepted warnings retaining full strength, and Star Chart organization. Check actual interactions and pixels, then obtain human feedback before implementation planning or live laptop integration.
steps.waiting_on: Setup mockup Refinement 2: keep the revised provider, gear and Cave sidebar layout for the laptop implementation plan, or refine it?

steps.name: Review Setup before laptop integration
steps.done_when: Settle the provider mockup and review the Setup walkthrough before implementation planning and live laptop integration. The accepted warning default is only one policy decision; further mockup feedback remains open and a slice closes only on John's explicit instruction.

steps.name: Test providers in the running laptop Anchor
steps.done_when: After the provider mockup is settled and implementation work is agreed, test the provider flow in the current Anchor client actually running on John's laptop. Check the selected mother ship, subscriptions and optional API connections, per-account tests and honestly reported allowance/cost, warnings preserving full strength and explicit model changes. Distinguish the actual laptop client from fresh-browser mockup checks; do not reset first-time setup or disrupt ongoing sessions.

steps.name: Second: connect subscriptions and optional API keys
steps.done_when: After host connection, show a provider checklist allowing multiple separately named subscriptions per provider and optional API connections. Normal sign-in, credentials, tests and usage reports belong to the mother ship; show per-connection capacity, cost and honest unknowns.

steps.name: Wire Cave controls and reopen Setup
steps.done_when: After provider mockup settlement and laptop testing, wire the bottom of the Cave of Wonders left side window to the agreed mother-ship provider/model/reasoning settings. Retain the separately specified lower-right capacity display. After first-time Setup, show a gear at the far upper left and move the Anchor icon slightly right. The gear opens the same Setup page to modify existing settings and preserves completed host/provider/project setup. Verify in the running laptop client; credentials and tests stay on the mother ship.

steps.name: Optional: connect calendars and email
steps.done_when: After provider setup, expose a separate optional calendars/email button for Outlook and Gmail. Secure sign-in and integration run on the mother ship; this does not block independent personal-host or goal organization work.

steps.name: Backups and restore
steps.done_when: Set up backups from the chosen project mapping and main directory.
